title: Solvability of Sₐ is Downward Closed Under Injections
description: The parent proved the intrinsic threshold IsSolvable (Perm α) ↔ Fintype.card α ≤ 4. This entry extracts the order-structural consequence the threshold form hides: solvability of permutation groups is monotone in the carrier. The structural reason is perm_solvable_of_embedding — an embedding α ↪ β realizes Perm α as a subgroup of Perm β through Mathlib's injective hom Equiv.Perm.viaEmbeddingHom, so solvability of the larger permutation group descends to the smaller, with NO cardinality count and NO classification. From it, perm_solvable_mono and alternating_solvable_mono give the cardinality face (card α ≤ card β ∧ solvable β ⟹ solvable α), and solvable_perm_card_isDownSet packages {n | IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n))} as the down-set {0,1,2,3,4}. The embedding route and the arithmetic threshold route agree (mono_routes_agree): abstract subgroup descent and the down-closedness of n ≤ 4 are the same statement.

overview.historicalContext: That Sₘ is a subgroup of Sₙ for m ≤ n — fix the last n − m points and permute the first m — is one of the oldest observations about symmetric groups, and the immediate reason the solvable-by-radicals threshold cannot rise as the degree grows: once S₅ is non-solvable, every Sₙ with n ≥ 5 inherits a non-solvable subgroup and so is itself non-solvable. The parent entry phrased the Galois/Ruffini–Abel classification as an iff with Fintype.card α ≤ 4 on a single carrier. The monotonicity that makes that threshold a genuine down-set — solvable on a small set whenever solvable on a larger one — is logically prior to the exact value 4, and is what this entry isolates and formalizes.
overview.problemStatement: Show that solvability of the symmetric group is monotone in its carrier: whenever an embedding α ↪ β exists and Perm β is solvable, Perm α is solvable too — a purely structural descent along Mathlib's injective hom Equiv.Perm.viaEmbeddingHom, with no cardinality counting — and package the solvable cardinalities as the down-set {0,1,2,3,4}.
overview.proofStrategy: The descent runs through a single structural lemma, `perm_solvable_of_embedding`: an embedding `e : α ↪ β` induces the injective homomorphism `Equiv.Perm.viaEmbeddingHom e : Perm α →* Perm β`, and solvability is inherited by (injective preimages of) subgroups, so `IsSolvable (Perm β)` forces `IsSolvable (Perm α)`. The cardinality corollary `perm_solvable_mono` is then one line: for finite types `card α ≤ card β` produces an embedding via `Function.Embedding.nonempty_of_card_le`. Finally `mono_routes_agree` verifies this subgroup-descent route coincides with the arithmetic route read off the parent threshold `perm_solvable_iff_card`, and the whole picture is packaged as the down-set `{0,1,2,3,4}` (`solvable_perm_card_isDownSet`).
overview.modernSignificance: Carrier-monotonicity is the functorial content of the classification: Perm is a functor from the category of finite sets and injections to groups, and IsSolvable is a property of groups closed under subgroups, so solvability of permutation groups is a contravariant (downward) property in the carrier. Stating it via Equiv.Perm.viaEmbeddingHom keeps the proof free of any cardinality count — it is the abstract reason behind the numerical threshold, not a corollary of it. The down-set packaging (4 is the maximum solvable cardinality) is the order-theoretic shadow of S₅ being the minimal non-solvable symmetric group, the seed of Abel–Ruffini.
keyInsights: **The descent is structural, not numerical.** `perm_solvable_of_embedding` derives solvability of `Perm α` from solvability of `Perm β` using only that `Equiv.Perm.viaEmbeddingHom e` is an *injective* homomorphism `Perm α →* Perm β` and that solvability passes to subgroups (`solvable_of_solvable_injective`). No cardinality is counted — the implication is the abstract reason the threshold exists, logically prior to the value 4.

**Cardinality-monotonicity is a one-line corollary.** For finite types, `card α ≤ card β` produces an embedding `α ↪ β` (`Function.Embedding.nonempty_of_card_le`), so `perm_solvable_mono` is just the embedding descent fed that embedding. The alternating version `alternating_solvable_mono` rides the parent bridge `alternating_solvable_iff_sym_solvable` in both directions, reducing to the symmetric case.

**Two routes, one fact.** `mono_routes_agree` shows the abstract subgroup-descent implication coincides with the purely arithmetic one read off the parent threshold `perm_solvable_iff_card` (where the whole content collapses to `omega` on `card ≤ 4`). 'Solvability descends along injections' and '`n ≤ 4` is downward closed' are the same statement viewed two ways.

**The solvable cardinalities form the down-set {0,1,2,3,4}.** `solvable_perm_card_eq_le_four` rewrites `IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n)) ↔ n ≤ 4`, `solvable_perm_card_isDownSet` states the closure under `m ≤ n`, and `four_is_max_solvable_card` pins 4 as the maximum — the order-theoretic shadow of S₅ being the minimal non-solvable symmetric group.

**Why the threshold cannot rise with degree.** Because every Sₘ embeds in Sₙ for m ≤ n, once S₅ is non-solvable every Sₙ (n ≥ 5) contains a non-solvable subgroup and is non-solvable. Monotonicity is exactly what turns the single non-solvable witness S₅ into the unbounded family that makes Abel–Ruffini bite in every degree ≥ 5.

conclusion.summary: Isolates and formalizes the carrier-monotonicity hidden in the parent's threshold `IsSolvable (Perm α) ↔ card α ≤ 4`. The core `perm_solvable_of_embedding` descends solvability along any injection `α ↪ β` via the injective hom `Equiv.Perm.viaEmbeddingHom`, with no cardinality count; from it follow the cardinality-monotone forms (symmetric and alternating), the route-agreement theorem identifying structural descent with arithmetic down-closedness, and the packaging of {n | IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n))} as the down-set {0,1,2,3,4} with maximum 4. Fully verified, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Recasts the Abel–Ruffini threshold as a genuine order-theoretic down-set rather than an isolated numerical bound: solvability is a contravariant (downward) property of the carrier under the functor Perm, so the single non-solvable witness S₅ propagates to every higher degree by subgroup inheritance. The embedding route shows this is structural — true of any subgroup-closed property — and independent of the exact value 4, which is supplied separately by the parent classification.
openQuestions: Generalize the embedding descent from `IsSolvable` to other subgroup-closed group properties (nilpotency, supersolvability), exhibiting a uniform 'property is contravariant in the carrier' statement.
Formalize the functoriality explicitly: package Perm as a functor from finite sets with injections to groups and carrier-monotonicity as the contravariance of a subgroup-closed predicate along it.
State the analogous down-set/threshold result for the alternating groups directly (the minimal non-solvable alternating group A₅), parallel to the symmetric `four_is_max_solvable_card`.

mathlibDependencies.description: An embedding e : α ↪ β as a group hom Perm α →* Perm β: a permutation of α is extended by the identity off the image of e. The functorial action of Perm on injections.
viaEmbeddingHom e is injective, so it realizes Perm α as a subgroup of Perm β. The hinge of the structural descent.
An injective group hom f : G →* G' with G' solvable forces G solvable (G embeds as a subgroup of a solvable group). Composed with viaEmbeddingHom_injective to descend solvability.
For finite types, Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card β yields a (nonempty) embedding α ↪ β. Converts the cardinality hypothesis into the embedding the structural lemma consumes.

mainTheorems.name: perm_solvable_of_embedding
mainTheorems.description: Structural descent: an embedding α ↪ β makes Perm α a subgroup of Perm β (via the injective hom viaEmbeddingHom), so IsSolvable (Perm β) forces IsSolvable (Perm α). No cardinality, no classification.

mainTheorems.name: perm_solvable_mono
mainTheorems.description: Cardinality monotonicity for symmetric groups: Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card β and IsSolvable (Perm β) force IsSolvable (Perm α).
mainTheorems.leanType: [Fintype α] → [Fintype β] → (Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card β) → [IsSolvable (Perm β)] → IsSolvable (Perm α)

mainTheorems.description: Cardinality monotonicity for alternating groups, obtained from the symmetric case through the parent bridge alternating_solvable_iff_sym_solvable.
mainTheorems.leanType: (Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card β) → IsSolvable (alternatingGroup β) → IsSolvable (alternatingGroup α)

mainTheorems.name: mono_routes_agree
mainTheorems.description: The embedding route and the arithmetic threshold route prove the same implication: under card α ≤ card β, solvable β ⟹ solvable α, derived here purely from perm_solvable_iff_card and omega.
mainTheorems.leanType: (Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card β) → (IsSolvable (Perm β) → IsSolvable (Perm α))

mainTheorems.name: solvable_perm_card_isDownSet
mainTheorems.description: The solvable cardinalities are downward closed: m ≤ n and IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n)) force IsSolvable (Perm (Fin m)).
mainTheorems.leanType: {m n : ℕ} → (m ≤ n) → IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n)) → IsSolvable (Perm (Fin m))

mainTheorems.name: four_is_max_solvable_card
mainTheorems.description: 4 is the largest cardinality with solvable symmetric group: Perm (Fin 4) is solvable, and any solvable Perm (Fin n) has n ≤ 4.

mainTheorems.statement: An embedding α ↪ β with Perm β solvable forces Perm α solvable — solvability of permutation groups is downward closed under injections.

sections.title: §1 Structural monotonicity along an embedding
sections.summary: perm_solvable_of_embedding: solvable_of_solvable_injective applied to viaEmbeddingHom_injective e. An embedding realizes Perm α as a subgroup of Perm β, and solvability descends — with no mention of cardinality.
sections.mathContext: Perm is functorial on injections: e : α ↪ β induces an injective group hom Perm α →* Perm β by extending permutations with the identity off im e. Solvability is closed under subgroups, hence flows from codomain to domain.

sections.title: §2 The cardinality face
sections.summary: perm_solvable_mono converts card α ≤ card β into an embedding (Function.Embedding.nonempty_of_card_le) and applies §1; alternating_solvable_mono transports the conclusion across the parent bridge to alternating groups.
sections.mathContext: A finite type embeds into another exactly when its cardinality is no larger, so the structural descent of §1 is precisely cardinality monotonicity once an embedding is produced.

sections.title: §3 Route agreement
sections.summary: mono_routes_agree re-derives the monotone implication arithmetically: rewrite hypothesis and goal through the parent threshold perm_solvable_iff_card, leaving card β ≤ 4 → card α ≤ 4 under card α ≤ card β, closed by omega. The structural descent of §1–2 and this arithmetic prove the same implication.
sections.mathContext: The abstract subgroup-descent route explains why solvability is monotone; the arithmetic route, consuming the parent threshold as a black box, pins the boundary — the two agree by mono_routes_agree.

sections.title: §4 The down-set packaging
sections.summary: solvable_perm_card_eq_le_four (IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n)) ↔ n ≤ 4), solvable_perm_card_isDownSet (downward closure on ℕ), and four_is_max_solvable_card (4 is the maximum, with witness Perm (Fin 4) solvable) present {n | solvable (Perm (Fin n))} = {0,1,2,3,4} as a bounded down-set.
sections.mathContext: The threshold n ≤ 4 is downward closed and bounded by 4, so it is the down-set with maximum 4 — the order-theoretic shadow of S₅ being the minimal non-solvable symmetric group.
